So why are so many Africans choosing Nairobi? Here are the facts. Number one. Since January twenty twenty-five, Kenya lets citizens of every African country except Somalia and Libya enter without an electronic travel authorisation, and stay for up to two months. That includes Nigerians. Number two. Jobs. The Nigerian news site Legit lists Kenya among the top new destinations for Nigerians, because Nairobi is a hub for tech, start-ups, finance and international organisations. Number three. Rent. A one-bedroom in Nairobi costs about three hundred and fifteen to four hundred and fifty dollars a month, paid monthly. In Lagos, it is about four hundred to six hundred dollars or more, and landlords often ask for one or two years upfront. Number four. Power and internet. In a comparison of five African cities by NaijaSabi, Lagos had the weakest power supply, so many people pay for generators. Nairobi has fast, affordable fibre internet.

So why don't Kenyans move to Lagos? It is not because Nigeria is a bad place. Lagos is one of the most exciting cities in Africa. But Kenyans who go abroad mostly head to the Gulf, the United States and the United Kingdom, for jobs and better pay. And Nigeria's own economy is pushing many Nigerians out. They even have a word for it. Japa. So for East Africans looking for work, Lagos is not the obvious magnet. For now, Nairobi is.

Kenya and Nigeria are not enemies. We are friends who love to argue online. So, Nigerians, would you move to Kenya? Kenyans, would you move to Lagos? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe to NEXTSCENE TV for more.
